example.t: Our clocks **went back** on Sunday, so our call is now **an hour later for you**: three **my time**, six **your time**. **Does that still work for you?**
Hmm, I have to pick up my kids at six. **Could we make it** three **my time**? **That's** twelve **your time**.
Sorry, that's my lunch break. **What about** eleven **my time**? **That's** two **your time**.
I've got a doctor's appointment at two. **Could we make it** four **my time**? **That's** one **your time**.
Great, one **works for me**! So that's one **my time**, four **your time**.

blocks.instr: Now discuss: is changing the clocks worth it? Use the box.
items: **1**  Name **two** ways the clock change affects you or people you know: sleep, kids, pets, work calls…
**2**  Does it do more harm than good? Give **two** reasons.
**3**  Summer time or winter time all year: which would you keep, and why?
blocks.fast: If you're done: who do you talk to in other time zones? Tell your partner what time it is there now: “It's … my time, … their time.”
